YOUR INVESTIGATION

It worked on my first try.

Expected: every true crossing collects once; a near miss collects nothing. Why does normal movement pass while a fast crossing fails?

  1. Compare normal and fast movement
  2. Inspect previous and current positions
  3. Try a larger hitbox; challenge it with regression
  4. Fix path detection and verify all five cases

Evidence & candidate fixes

Green outlines show the original bounds. Blue outlines and the connecting line show previous → current positions. Amber marks the active pickup area. A fast crossing can miss at both endpoints.

Run a replay to capture the crossing.

// Original: observes only the final position
collectIf(overlaps(current, coin));
// Quick patch: still checks only the endpoint
collectIf(overlaps(current, expand(coin, 20)));
// Proper fix: check the path, keep real bounds
collectIf(crosses(previous, current, coin));
// Award only if not already collected.

The quick patch must survive more than its original reproduction.

Recorded replays isolate horizontal pickup by pausing gravity. The frame hitch models a 180ms movement gap; it does not slow your browser. Manual play and replays use the same pickup detector. Passing these five cases does not establish production game readiness.
